h1: The 6 Best Office Supply Carts Under $100 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Supply Carts Under $100: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: six rolling office supply carts under $100, compared on tiers, drawers, wheels and listed weight capacity.
summary: The Goovilla 3 Tier is the best office supply cart under $100, the only one stating a weight capacity at 124 lbs, plus a removable top drawer, for under $25. The SUNALLY wins for sorting small supplies with eight drawers. The YASONIC offers heavy-duty wheels, and the ZOES fits the tightest gaps.
intro: Cheap rolling carts all look alike in photos, and the mistake is buying on tier count. What separates a cart you like from one that wobbles is the frame material, the wheels and whether the listing states a weight rating. Most sellers in this price range skip that number, and a missing rating is a signal worth reading.

We reviewed rolling carts under $100 and ranked them on listed capacity, drawers, wheels and frame details. Four are three-tier utility carts, one is a drawer unit, and one is a mixed plastic and iron build. Every one lands in the $25 to $50 bucket or lower, so the question is not budget but which cart tells you the most about what it can hold.

products.name: Goovilla 3 Tier Rolling Utility Cart Organizer with Removable Drawer
products.verdict: A stated 124 lb capacity and a removable top drawer.
products.description:
The Goovilla is a three-tier rolling cart with a removable drawer on top and safety protection on the wheels. The listing says it holds up to 124 lbs for daily use, and it costs under $25. The removable drawer is practical: you carry pens, tape and small supplies to your desk without moving the whole cart.

The stated weight rating is what puts it first. Most carts here give no number at all, so you cannot judge them. The SUNALLY and YASONIC cost a bracket more yet list no capacity, and the other three under $25 are equally vague. A number is not a guarantee, but it is something to hold the seller to.

Buy it for everyday desk-side storage. The caveat is that it has open tiers and a single drawer, with the frame material unstated, so it will not sort small items like the SUNALLY.

products.name: SUNALLY Rolling Cart With 8 Drawers,Storage Drawer Cart for Craft Art,Green
products.verdict: Eight drawers on a powder-coated steel frame.
products.description:
The SUNALLY is a rolling cart with eight drawers on a powder-coated steel frame, in the $25 to $50 range. Powder coating bonds a tough finish to the metal, so it resists chips and rust better than basic paint. Eight drawers are the real feature, because small items such as washi tape, markers and clips vanish on open shelves.

It ranks second because drawers sort supplies far better than open tiers do, though the listing states no weight rating, which the Goovilla does. It also costs a bracket more. Against the three-tier carts below, it trades open shelf space for organization.

Buy it for craft supplies, stationery and anything small. The caveat is capacity: with no listed rating, do not stack heavy books or equipment on top. It also comes in green only, which may clash with a formal office.

products.name: YASONIC 3 Tier Metal Rolling Cart
products.verdict: A metal 3-tier cart with 2 inch heavy-duty wheels.
products.description:
The YASONIC is a three-tier metal rolling cart with a coated frame and 2 inch heavy-duty wheels, in the $25 to $50 range. Wheel size is the spec that matters under load. A larger wheel rolls over thresholds, cables and carpet edges that stop small casters.

It ranks third because the listing stresses wheels and frame, which are the right things to emphasize, but gives no weight rating. Against the Goovilla it costs a bracket more and states no capacity, though its metal frame is described in more detail. Its coating resists scratches in a way plastic shelves cannot.

Buy it for heavier loads in a home office, such as reams of paper, a printer or equipment. The caveat is that missing capacity number: check the product page before loading it to the limit.
products.idealFor: Heavier loads on a rolling cart.
products.skipIf: You want a stated weight rating.

products.name: ZOES HOMEWARE 3 Tier Metal Rolling Cart on Wheels,Heavy Duty Utility Cart
products.verdict: A 16 by 12 inch footprint with a durable frame and strong wheels.
products.description:
The ZOES HOMEWARE is a three-tier metal cart that occupies only 16 inches by 12 inches of floor space, with a durable frame and strong wheels. It costs under $25. That footprint is narrower than a typical drawer unit, so it can slip into the gap between a desk and a wall.

It ranks fourth because the small size caps what you can store, and the listing gives no weight rating. Against the YASONIC, it is cheaper and smaller, with less emphasis on wheel size. Against the Goovilla, it matches the price but cannot match the removable drawer or the stated capacity.

Buy it for tight spaces beside a desk or in a small apartment office. The caveat is size: the shelves are modest, so big binders, boxes and tall items will not fit comfortably.

products.name: 3 Tier Rolling Utility Cart with Drawer,REBECAT Utility Cart Made of
products.verdict: A 3-tier cart with a drawer and shelves that save space.
products.description:
The REBECAT is a three-tier rolling utility cart with a drawer and shelves designed to save space, in the under $25 bucket. A drawer on a cart this cheap is helpful because it keeps small items from sliding off the shelf during a roll.

It ranks fifth because it matches the Goovilla's drawer idea at the same price, but the listing gives no weight rating and the product title is cut off. That limits what can be said about it. There is nothing wrong on paper, but nothing that sets it above the Goovilla, which states a capacity.

Buy it for small storage jobs on a budget. The caveat is limited detail, so read the full manufacturer page, and look for the frame material and any weight limit before ordering.
products.idealFor: Small storage jobs on a budget.

products.name: Sywhitta 3-Tier Plastic Rolling Utility Cart with Wheels for Storage,Black
products.verdict: A plastic and iron-pipe cart with 360 degree wheels.
products.description:
The Sywhitta is a three-tier cart made of plastic and iron pipe, with four wheels that rotate 360 degrees and a handle, in the under $25 bucket. Four swivel wheels let you steer in any direction without turning the whole cart, which helps in a cramped office.

It ranks last because plastic shelves are the tradeoff next to the metal carts above. Plastic can bow under books and heavy supplies, and the listing gives no weight rating. The iron pipe frame adds some structure, but the shelf material limits what you can place on it.

Buy it for light storage like paper, art supplies or cleaning items. The caveat is construction: skip it if you want an all-metal cart, or if you plan to store anything heavy.

whatMatters.detail: Weight capacity is the load the cart can carry. It matters for books, printers and boxed supplies. Look for a number in pounds in the title or bullets. Only the Goovilla lists one here, at 124 lbs. A missing number is not proof of a weak cart, but you cannot plan a load around it, and you have little recourse if a shelf bows.

Frame material decides how the cart ages. Metal resists flexing, and powder coating protects against rust, while plastic shelves can sag over time. The SUNALLY lists powder-coated steel and the Sywhitta plastic with iron pipe. Check the listing for steel or metal wording and the finish, and be cautious when the material is unstated, because thin tubing and plastic joints fail first.

Wheels decide how easily the cart rolls under a load. A larger wheel handles thresholds and carpet better. The YASONIC lists 2 inch heavy-duty wheels and the Sywhitta four 360 degree casters. Check the wheel size and whether any lock, and consider your floor surface before you buy, since hard floors forgive small casters and carpet does not.

Drawers sort small supplies and hide clutter, while open tiers handle bulkier items. The SUNALLY lists eight, and the Goovilla and REBECAT carry one drawer each. Choose by how much small stuff you own. If your supplies are mostly pens, tape and clips, drawers pay for themselves quickly, while bulky items still need open shelves.

A smaller footprint fits beside a desk without blocking a chair or a door. The ZOES lists 16 by 12 inches. Measure your gap first, including the swing of any doors, and compare it with the listing. Many listings omit dimensions, so check the manufacturer page for width and depth.

faq.q: How much weight can these carry?
faq.a: Only the Goovilla lists a figure, up to 124 lbs. For the others, including the YASONIC and SUNALLY, check the product page before loading heavy items such as printers or paper boxes.
Buying by tier count alone. Frame material, wheel quality and a stated capacity matter more. The Goovilla stands out for listing 124 lbs, while many three-tier carts say nothing at all.

faq.q: Is the SUNALLY worth it over a 3-tier cart?
faq.a: If you store many small items, yes. The SUNALLY has eight drawers that sort supplies better than open shelves. For books and bulky gear, a three-tier cart like the Goovilla is more practical.

The listings we reviewed do not say. Most carts like the Goovilla or YASONIC are flat-packed, so check the product page for assembly details and tools required before you order, and allow time for building.

The YASONIC lists 2 inch heavy-duty wheels and the Sywhitta lists 360 degree wheels, but the listings do not discuss carpet. Small wheels struggle on thick pile, so test it with a light load first and avoid pulling it over thick rugs or door tracks.

The listings do not address outdoor use. Metal carts like the SUNALLY have a powder-coated frame, but rain and humidity can still damage them, so check the manufacturer's guidance before leaving one outside, and store it dry.

finalTake: Buy the Goovilla if you want a cart with a number behind it: 124 lbs, for under $25. Craft and supply hoarders should take the SUNALLY for its eight drawers, and heavier loads suit the YASONIC. If your gap beside the desk is narrow, measure first and consider the 16 by 12 inch ZOES.
